text: Professor Ansel Thwaite. Mind the trench, I've been digging since dawn.
The First Tide! Fascinating people. Terrible taste in gods.
Every stone on these keys has writing on it, if you know how to look.
Is that... a relic? Bring it here, bring it here!
{relics} of seven! Remarkable. Let me see what's still missing.
Listen to that thunder. Nobody sane is at sea tonight.
Storm's right on top of us. Stay in the dry a while.
Every timber in the harbour's groaning. Ugly night.
Wretched rain. Gets into everything.
Rain again. Good for the cisterns, bad for the soul.
You're dripping on my floor, by the way.
Late to be wandering about.
Night's when the cursed come walking. Keep a lantern lit.
Can't sleep either, eh?
Up with the gulls, I see.
Early start, {player}.
Mist'll burn off by mid-morning.

options.label: I have something for you to read.
Tell me about the Lantern Court.

text: Sea people. Scales tattooed on their skin, cities on the islands before the islands were small.
They believed the tide was alive and could be spoken to. Then, by every account, it spoke back.
Coins, mostly. The odd tablet. Once, a whole jaw. Not human. I've stopped digging in that trench.
The antiquarian buys the coins. I keep the tablets. We have an arrangement.
Collectors. Rich ones. Buying every scrap of the First Tide for thirty years, through a dozen agents.
I've had offers for my notes. Large ones. I've refused them all, so far.
